title: Class 3B
synopsis: A completely normal school class becomes the most chaotic class in the country when their teacher announces a simple group assignment. Between cheating, conspiracy theories, a student election and one teacher who has completely lost patience, nobody gets the peaceful school day they expected.

scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.text: Class 3B was not the worst class in the school. According to Mr. Okoro, that was only because Class 3C had burned down a table the previous week. On Monday morning, everything was about to become much worse.

scenes.speaker: teacher
scenes.text: Your assignment is simple. Work in groups of three, research a topic, and present it on Friday.

scenes.speaker: jay
scenes.text: Sir, can I work alone? I don't trust other people with my marks.

scenes.speaker: teacher
scenes.text: Jay, you failed your last test because you wrote your name in the answer section.

scenes.speaker: musa
scenes.text: Sir, put me with Jay. I think we can create something powerful.

scenes.speaker: chika
scenes.text: No. If I am getting an A, I need intelligent people in my group.

scenes.speaker: musa
scenes.text: Then why are you still talking to us?

scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.text: The groups were assigned. Jay, Musa and Chika were together. Chika immediately regretted everything. Jay immediately went to sleep. Musa immediately announced that he had a plan.

scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.text: After school, the three students met to work on their assignment. Chika brought books. Jay brought nothing. Musa brought a strange confidence that suggested he had never completed an assignment in his life.

scenes.speaker: chika
scenes.text: We need to choose a topic and actually research it.

scenes.speaker: musa
scenes.text: I already have a better idea. We fake the entire thing.

scenes.speaker: chika
scenes.text: No.

scenes.speaker: jay
scenes.text: I support the fake thing.

scenes.speaker: chika
scenes.text: Of course you do.

scenes.speaker: musa
scenes.text: Relax. I know a guy who can make the presentation look professional.

scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.text: The presentation was supposed to be about renewable energy. Instead, Musa accidentally hired a man who believed renewable energy meant energy that renewed itself every morning.

scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.text: The next morning, Principal Ada announced that the school would hold a class representative election. Class 3B immediately became interested because nobody had ever explained what the representative actually did.

scenes.speaker: teacher
scenes.text: The class representative will communicate student concerns to the school.

scenes.speaker: musa
scenes.text: Does that mean power?

scenes.speaker: teacher
scenes.text: No.

scenes.speaker: musa
scenes.text: Then why are we voting?

scenes.speaker: chika
scenes.text: I am running because I actually care about the class.

scenes.speaker: jay
scenes.text: I am running because Musa said the winner gets to skip morning assembly.

scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.text: Musa launched his campaign five minutes later. His slogan was simple: 'Vote Musa. I will probably do something.' Nobody knew what the something was, but somehow the campaign was winning.

scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.text: Friday arrived. Chika had prepared a serious presentation. Jay had memorized one sentence. Musa had brought a laptop that was not his and a presentation that was about nuclear power instead of renewable energy.

scenes.speaker: teacher
scenes.text: Group three, you may begin.

scenes.speaker: chika
scenes.text: Our topic is renewable energy and how it can improve communities.

scenes.speaker: jay
scenes.text: Renewable energy is energy that comes back.

scenes.speaker: chika
scenes.text: Technically, yes.

scenes.speaker: musa
scenes.text: And now, nuclear weapons.

scenes.speaker: teacher
scenes.text: Why are there nuclear weapons on your renewable energy presentation?

scenes.speaker: musa
scenes.text: Because technically, sir, they are also very energetic.

scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.text: The presentation was immediately stopped. Principal Ada entered the classroom after hearing an explosion from the projector. She expected discipline. Instead, she found three students arguing about whether the explosion had improved their grade.

scenes.speaker: principal
scenes.text: Who caused this?

scenes.speaker: musa
scenes.text: The projector.

scenes.speaker: teacher
scenes.text: Musa.

scenes.speaker: musa
scenes.text: Fine. The projector and I worked together.

scenes.speaker: principal
scenes.text: All three of you are receiving detention.

scenes.speaker: jay
scenes.text: Can we appeal?

scenes.speaker: principal
scenes.text: You can appeal after detention.

scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.text: By lunchtime, the election results were announced. Against every reasonable expectation, Musa had won by three votes. Nobody understood how. Musa himself looked surprised.

scenes.speaker: teacher
scenes.text: Musa is now the class representative.

scenes.speaker: musa
scenes.text: I would like to thank everyone who voted for me, everyone who feared me, and the three people who I paid.

scenes.speaker: chika
scenes.text: You admitted bribing people.

scenes.speaker: musa
scenes.text: Yes. I am very transparent.

scenes.speaker: teacher
scenes.text: Your first responsibility is to report student concerns.

scenes.speaker: musa
scenes.text: I have one concern. This school has too much school.

scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.text: The class cheered. Mr. Okoro stared at the ceiling and questioned every decision that had brought him to Class 3B. Then the school bell rang, and Musa announced his first official policy: Friday was now a holiday.
